notes: §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR1: 'A SORT statement may appear anywhere in the Procedure Division except in the declarative portion.' SortBindFile calls SortBinder.ScreenDeclarativePlacement, which refuses a file SORT in a USE AFTER ERROR section (COBOL2700, the witness's case). Two departures at 85. (1) Rejects legal source: VersionConformancePass.GateSortMergeProcedures refuses a file SORT written inside another SORT's or MERGE's input or output procedure with COBOL2700 at every edition (its BoundSort arm is outside the Year >= 2023 block; kb/Work PB1139 decided it on the 2002-and-later rule), but the 1985 rule admits it anywhere outside the declaratives and §1985:XI.4.4.4 GR7 and GR10 forbid only executing one ('The range of the input procedure must not cause the execution of any MERGE, RETURN, or SORT statement'), so a SORT on a path never executed is legal 1985 source; the MERGE twin is already gated to 2023. (2) Under-rejects: a USE FOR DEBUGGING section is collected by ProcedureTableBuilder.DeclCollectSection without a BoundDeclarative, so BinderContext.DeclarativeAtCursor answers null there and a SORT in a debugging section compiles and runs. Probes at --std 85: (b) SORT nested two IFs deep in a USE AFTER ERROR section: COBOL2700; SORT in a main-line paragraph PERFORMed from the declaratives: compiles (lexical rule, correct); SORT in a debugging declarative: no diagnostic, executed (M2E); (c) a Format 2 table SORT (2002): COBOL0870; SORT inside an output procedure under IF FLG = 'Q' (never true): COBOL2700 (S4A); (e) sequential USING/GIVING. Classes a, d and f do not reach a placement rule. kb/Work PB5274 PB5275 holds the defects (code read: coderead-85/out-pipe/slice-47.json).

next.reason: 1985: "A SORT statement may appear anywhere in the Procedure Division except in the declarative portion."; 2023: "shall not appear in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement, in an input or output procedure, or in a". Both bar SORT in declaratives. Judged on this rule's text alone, 2023 also bars SORT in input or output procedures, which the 1985 'anywhere' wording allowed.
